semantic_correction.stem: Which self-care plan should the nurse recommend to an adult experiencing ongoing work-related stress?

options.A: Get enough sleep, stay physically active, make time to unwind, and stay connected with supportive people.
options.B: Protect work time by cutting sleep and social time until the stressful period has completely passed.
options.C: Stop regular physical activity during stressful weeks and resume it when the workload returns to normal.
options.D: Rely on alcohol to unwind in the evening instead of using relaxation practices or social support.

semantic_correction.rationale: CDC guidance updated May 12, 2026 recommends healthy daily coping strategies for stress, including adequate sleep, regular physical activity, making time to unwind with practices such as deep breathing, stretching, meditation, journaling, or relaxing activities, and connecting with trusted people or community supports. CDC also advises limiting alcohol rather than using it as a primary coping strategy. Therefore option A best reflects current evidence-based stress-management teaching.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Identify evidence-based health behaviors that support stress management and well-being: adequate sleep, physical activity, deliberate relaxation, and supportive social connection.
semantic_correction.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
semantic_correction.source_locator: Healthy ways to cope with stress — Take care of your mind: make time to unwind, deep breathing/stretching/meditation, relaxing activities; Connect with others: talk with trusted people and community supports; Take care of your body: get enough sleep, move more, limit alcohol intake
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: CDC recommends adequate sleep, physical activity, relaxation/unwinding practices, supportive social connection, and limiting alcohol as healthy stress-management strategies.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: shortened and balanced the correct answer, updated the source to CDC's May 12, 2026 guidance, and rebuilt distractors around sleep restriction, exercise avoidance, and alcohol reliance.

audit_findings_append.source_locator: Managing Stress — Healthy ways to cope with stress, updated May 12, 2026
audit_findings_append.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — wellness/coping education
audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item directly tests current healthy stress-management behaviors without a correct-answer length cue.

option_audit.A: Correct. Each component is directly supported by current CDC stress-management guidance.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. CDC emphasizes adequate sleep and social connection rather than sacrificing them during prolonged stress.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. CDC recommends physical activity as part of healthy coping and emotional well-being.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. CDC advises limiting alcohol and using healthy coping strategies instead.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone combines the CDC-supported stress-management domains tested in the stem.
cueing_check: All four choices are stress-management plans of comparable length and specificity; no unique-length or absolute-word cue identifies A.
